english_pairs.label: correct
english_pairs.source: Maintain adequate oral hydration, aiming for at least two litres of fluid per day unless otherwise advised.
english_pairs.candidate: Drink enough fluids every day, at least two litres, unless you are told otherwise.

english_pairs.label: correct
english_pairs.source: Avoid strenuous physical activity and lifting objects heavier than 5 kg for 6 weeks after surgery.
english_pairs.candidate: For 6 weeks after the operation, do not do heavy physical work and do not lift anything heavier than 5 kg.

english_pairs.label: correct
english_pairs.source: Keep the surgical wound clean and dry; do not apply any creams, powders or oils to the area.
english_pairs.candidate: Keep the wound clean and dry. Do not put creams, powders or oils on it.

english_pairs.label: correct
english_pairs.source: Resume your normal diet gradually, starting with light, bland foods and avoiding spicy or fried items for the first week.
english_pairs.candidate: Go back to your usual food slowly. Begin with light, plain food and stay away from spicy or fried food during the first week.

english_pairs.label: correct
english_pairs.source: Monitor blood glucose before breakfast and at bedtime, and record each reading in the diary provided.
english_pairs.candidate: Check your blood sugar before breakfast and at bedtime. Write down every reading in the diary you were given.

english_pairs.label: correct
english_pairs.source: Elevate the affected leg on two pillows when sitting or lying down to reduce swelling.
english_pairs.candidate: When you sit or lie down, keep the affected leg raised on two pillows to bring down the swelling.

english_pairs.label: correct
english_pairs.source: Do not drive or operate machinery for 48 hours after the procedure, or while feeling drowsy.
english_pairs.candidate: Do not drive or use machines for 48 hours after the procedure, or at any time you feel drowsy.

english_pairs.label: correct
english_pairs.source: Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water before and after changing the dressing.
english_pairs.candidate: Before and after you change the dressing, wash your hands well with soap and water.

english_pairs.label: correct
english_pairs.source: Attend the surgical outpatient clinic in 10 days for wound review and suture removal.
english_pairs.candidate: Come to the surgery outpatient clinic after 10 days so the wound can be checked and the stitches removed.

english_pairs.label: correct
english_pairs.source: Repeat kidney function and electrolyte tests one week before the next appointment.
english_pairs.candidate: Have your kidney function and electrolyte tests done again one week before your next appointment.

english_pairs.label: correct
english_pairs.source: Cardiology review in 4 weeks with a fresh ECG; bring all previous reports and the discharge summary.
english_pairs.candidate: Visit the heart clinic after 4 weeks for a new ECG. Bring all your earlier reports and your discharge summary.

english_pairs.label: correct
english_pairs.source: Telephone the ward on the number provided if the follow-up appointment needs to be rescheduled.
english_pairs.candidate: If you need to change your follow-up appointment, call the ward on the number you were given.

english_pairs.label: correct
english_pairs.source: Seek immediate medical attention if you experience chest tightness, breathlessness at rest or fainting.
english_pairs.candidate: Get medical help straight away if you have chest tightness, trouble breathing while resting, or if you faint.

english_pairs.label: correct
english_pairs.source: Return to hospital immediately if the wound edges separate, or if there is increasing redness, warmth or pus.
english_pairs.candidate: Come back to the hospital at once if the wound opens up, or if the redness, warmth or pus gets worse.

english_pairs.label: correct
english_pairs.source: Contact your doctor if the temperature stays above 38 degrees Celsius for more than 24 hours.
english_pairs.candidate: Call your doctor if your fever stays higher than 38 degrees Celsius for over 24 hours.

english_pairs.label: correct
english_pairs.source: Do not stop the breathing exercises even if you feel better; continue until the review.
english_pairs.candidate: Keep doing the breathing exercises until the review, even when you feel better.

english_pairs.label: correct

english_pairs.candidate: Eat several small meals through the day instead of three big meals.

english_pairs.label: correct
english_pairs.source: Restrict dietary sodium to under 2 grams daily and weigh yourself each morning, reporting a gain of more than 2 kg within 3 days.
english_pairs.candidate: Eat less than 2 grams of sodium a day. Weigh yourself every morning and report it if your weight goes up by more than 2 kg within 3 days.

english_pairs.label: correct
english_pairs.source: Sleep with the head end of the bed raised and avoid lying completely flat.
english_pairs.candidate: Keep the head of your bed raised when you sleep. Do not lie fully flat.

english_pairs.label: correct

english_pairs.candidate: For the first two weeks, get your blood pressure checked at the local health centre every other day.

simplify_sources.text: Ambulate with assistance at least three times daily to prevent venous stasis; avoid prolonged immobility.
Maintain a low-sodium, fluid-restricted diet (1.5 L/day) and report weight gain exceeding 2 kg within 72 hours.
Seek urgent medical review for any new-onset dyspnoea, orthopnoea or peripheral oedema.
Outpatient review with repeat renal function tests and a urine albumin-creatinine ratio in 6 weeks.
Refrain from over-the-counter preparations containing NSAIDs unless specifically authorised by the treating team.
Return to the casualty department if melaena, haematemesis or syncope occurs.
Perform incentive spirometry ten times every hour while awake for the first postoperative week.
Keep the incision site dry for 48 hours, after which showering is permitted but soaking in baths, pools or the sea should be avoided until fully healed.
Histopathology results will be discussed at the surgical clinic; please attend with a relative if possible.
Adhere to a diabetic diet with consistent carbohydrate distribution across meals and avoid refined sugars.
Report any episode of hypoglycaemia (sweating, tremor, confusion) or persistent hyperglycaemia above 300 mg/dL to the diabetes team.
Compression stockings should be worn during the day and removed at night for 6 weeks.
Suture removal at the primary health centre on day 10; if the wound appears inflamed earlier, attend sooner.
Avoid exposure to dust, smoke and known allergens; use a damp cloth for cleaning and keep windows closed on high-pollen days.
Persistent vomiting, inability to tolerate oral fluids, or reduced urine output for over 8 hours warrants immediate hospital attendance.
